<thought>Based on the dominant ion at m/z 180.0423, the most plausible adduct is [M+Na]⁺, giving a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈157.053 Da. The formula C₇H₉O₄ has an exact monoisotopic mass of 157.0501 Da, matching this mass within a few ppm and reproducing the observed ~10 % M+1 isotopic intensity (consistent with ~7 carbons). Therefore the molecular formula is C₇H₉O₄.</thought>
<final_answer>C7H9O4</final_answer>
